generated_for: Soma normal-chat Plugin/MCP UX research iteration 5
principles: Keep existing Soma runtime authorities and execution paths unchanged.
Split a public tool only when proven state, safety, confirmation, or external-world semantics differ materially.
Use human-facing titles, trigger-first descriptions, and ChatGPT invocation labels on every public tool.
Treat annotations as truthful host hints, never as server-side authorization.
Keep stateful helper operations out of readOnlyHint=true tools.
Keep canonical project memory distinct from repository wiki and legacy knowledge.
Do not add automatic commit, push, restart, refresh, plugin install, or other hidden side effects.

ssh_inspect.title: Inspect SSH host
ssh_inspect.description: Use this when you need to check whether an authorized SSH host, tunnel, or service is reachable, or inspect live read-only SSH health, environment, GPU telemetry, logs, files, services, Git, or Docker state. Do not use it to change the host.

docker_query.title: Inspect Docker
docker_query.description: Use this when you need Docker capabilities, health, container or Compose inspection without changing Docker state. Do not use it to start, stop, remove, or prune resources.

cloudflare_query.title: Inspect Cloudflare
cloudflare_query.description: Use this when you need authorized Cloudflare capabilities, health, DNS, ruleset, tunnel, cache, or zone information without changing Cloudflare.

ssh_action.title: Run SSH action
ssh_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants an authorized remote SSH command, reviewed script, root shell, administration change, transfer, deployment, or profile activation. This surface can change or remove remote state.
ssh_action.notes: Conservative C1 annotation: mixed remote execution risks remain one tool pending A/B.

run_start.title: Start durable command
run_start.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to run tests, scripts, PowerShell, or a Hermes operation as durable local or remote execution. The command surface is unrestricted enough to overwrite, delete, or reach external systems; do not use it for inspection.
run_start.notes: Conservative C1 annotation for unrestricted execution.

workflow_query.title: Inspect workflow
workflow_query.description: Use this when you need durable workflow status, events, or results without advancing or cancelling the workflow.

workflow_action.title: Control workflow
workflow_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to start or cancel a validated durable workflow. Workflow steps can launch allowlisted project commands that may write files.
workflow_action.notes: Conservative C1 annotation: configured project commands can write files and may execute code.

cancel_run.title: Cancel durable run
cancel_run.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to cancel one exact known durable run or PowerShell command group. Do not use it as a broad process-kill tool.

run_query.title: Inspect durable run
run_query.description: Use this when you need durable run status, input, output, events, terminal evidence, results, summaries, locks, or repository preflight without launching or cancelling work.

task_query.title: Inspect task
task_query.description: Use this when you need canonical task capabilities, status, result, events, links, or quarantine evidence without changing the task.

task_action.title: Control task
task_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to start, steer, supply input to, cancel, or resolve one canonical task. Task start delegates to the durable execution backend and can have unrestricted command effects.
task_action.notes: Conservative C1 annotation because start delegates to unrestricted durable execution.

system_query.title: Inspect Soma service
system_query.description: Use this when you need Soma capabilities, self-checks, configuration validation, local-model health, capability identity, or reload status without changing the running service.

system_action.title: Reload Soma service
system_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants a validated Soma module reload or last-known-good rollback. Do not use it for ordinary health or configuration inspection.

supervisor_query.title: Inspect supervisor
supervisor_query.description: Use this when you need durable supervisor status, events, results, notifications, or a resume prompt without advancing the supervisor.

supervisor_action.title: Control supervisor
supervisor_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to start, resume, pause, or cancel a durable supervisor. Start and resume can advance child execution; cancel can terminate an active child.
supervisor_action.notes: Conservative C1 annotation pending live confirmation-cost measurement.

trading_signal_submit.title: Record trading signal
trading_signal_submit.description: Use this when you need to store one packet-bound Trading Lab signal or NO_TRADE decision in the local journal. This tool does not submit a broker order.

trading_signal_get.title: Read trading signal
trading_signal_get.description: Use this when you need one exact Trading Lab signal record from the local journal.

trading_signal_list.title: List trading signals
trading_signal_list.description: Use this when you need a filtered page of Trading Lab signal records from the local journal.

trading_signal_cancel_before_entry.title: Cancel trading signal
trading_signal_cancel_before_entry.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to cancel one stored Trading Lab signal before entry. This changes the signal's durable lifecycle and does not close an existing broker position.
trading_signal_cancel_before_entry.notes: Conservative C1 lifecycle annotation; G-corpus measures whether host framing is excessive.

trading_companion_action.title: Advance trading companion
trading_companion_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to start, decide, review, or execute a Trading Lab companion cycle. Some stages read the configured provider and execute can reach broker-demo trading.
trading_companion_action.notes: Conservative C1 annotation for mixed internal/provider/execution stages.

trading_action_submit.title: Submit trading action
trading_action_submit.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants one guarded Trading Lab action such as entry, modification, close, flatten, or emergency close. The configured mode may be internal paper or broker-demo.
trading_action_submit.notes: Conservative C1 annotation; C2 paper/broker split is gated on G42-G44.

trading_runtime_control.title: Control trading runtime
trading_runtime_control.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to start, stop, change the kill switch, or run a manual trading supervision/analysis pass. Use Trading Lab record reads for runtime status instead of this mutation surface.
trading_runtime_control.notes: Conservative C1 annotation; provider-backed actions share this surface.

repo_query.title: Inspect repository
repo_query.description: Use this when you need to inspect or search a repository (repo) or repository evidence: current status, files, audit documents, source text, diffs, history, commit ranges, patch status, or the current state of an interrupted repository task. Do not use it to preview, apply, or commit changes.

repo_preview.title: Prepare repository change
repo_preview.description: Use this when the user asks to make, correct, edit, create, remove, or otherwise change repository source/files and you need a durable hash-bound preview or cleanup plan before applying it. This creates Soma preview state but does not modify repository files.

repo_apply.title: Apply repository change
repo_apply.description: Use this when the user has authorized an established managed preview, cleanup, revert, or move. This can overwrite, remove, restore, or move repository content; it does not push.

repo_commit.title: Commit selected files
repo_commit.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants a protected local branch creation or a commit containing selected validated files. Do not push or include unrelated work.

memory_query.title: Read project memory
memory_query.description: Use this when you need to resolve, search, retrieve, or check Soma's canonical project memory without creating a context packet or changing memory. Do not substitute repository wiki or MEMORY.md files.

memory_context.title: Build project-memory context
memory_context.description: Use this when you need a persisted context packet assembled from Soma's canonical project memory for a specific query. This creates durable Soma packet state but does not change the underlying memory records.

research_query.title: Read research evidence
research_query.description: Use this when you need stored research sources, claim evidence, questions, decisions, or research health without building a new context packet.

research_context.title: Build research context
research_context.description: Use this when you need research search results or a research context packet. Both operations currently persist a context-packet record, so this is intentionally not a read-only surface.

knowledge_query.title: Read repository knowledge
knowledge_query.description: Use this when you need the repository wiki or legacy repository-knowledge records. Do not use it for Soma's canonical project memory or for research context-packet construction.

memory_action.title: Update project memory
memory_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to bind, save, supersede, archive, reject, dispute, rebuild, sync, or deliberately adopt drift in Soma's canonical project memory. Some operations change memory authority or lifecycle.
memory_action.notes: C1 intentionally keeps ordinary and lifecycle memory writes together; G47/G48 gate a later split.

knowledge_action.title: Update repository knowledge
knowledge_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to refresh the repository wiki or change legacy/research knowledge records. Do not use it for Soma's canonical project-memory workflow.
knowledge_action.notes: Conservative because legacy supersede shares this surface.

ssh_query.title: Read SSH configuration
ssh_query.description: Use this when you need local SSH capability metadata, profile-change status, or configured project bindings. Do not use it to create a probe, preview, snapshot, or remote change.

ssh_prepare.title: Prepare SSH configuration
ssh_prepare.description: Use this when you need a sanitized credential-source probe or a durable SSH profile-change preview. This creates local Soma probe or preview state but does not mutate the remote host.

ssh_probe.title: Probe SSH host
ssh_probe.description: Use this when you need a fresh authorized host capability snapshot or project-binding validation. This performs remote read-only probes and persists local Soma evidence.

docker_action.title: Control Docker
docker_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants a bounded Docker build, pull, push, create, start, stop, restart, pause, unpause, Compose down, or exec action that is not in the destructive removal/prune class.

docker_destructive_action.title: Remove Docker resources
docker_destructive_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants a Docker kill, removal, prune, Compose removal, or volume-destructive action. These operations can discard containers, images, networks, volumes, or cached build state.

cloudflare_action.title: Update Cloudflare
cloudflare_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to change, update, or create authorized Cloudflare state, including DNS records, DNSSEC, cache purge, ruleset edits, Turnstile updates, or tunnel configuration, and the requested effect is not a deletion or secret rotation.

cloudflare_destructive_action.title: Delete Cloudflare resources
cloudflare_destructive_action.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants a Cloudflare deletion, DNS batch that may delete records, or Turnstile secret rotation. These operations can remove external configuration or invalidate an existing secret.

trading_journal_query.title: Read Trading Lab records
trading_journal_query.description: Use this when you need local Trading Lab packets, outcomes, rejections, reports, recorded actions, companion lists, runtime status, or other journal-backed evidence without contacting the market provider.

trading_market_query.title: Read live market data
trading_market_query.description: Use this when you need Trading Lab health, configuration with observed account state, symbols, specifications, ticks, candles, history, candle boundaries, or broker exposure from the configured MT5/provider path.

trading_companion_sync.title: Sync trading companion
trading_companion_sync.description: Use this when you need one Trading Lab companion record refreshed against its current signal, action, and outcome links. The default sync path updates durable journal links before returning the record.
trading_companion_sync.notes: New Iteration-5 correction: companion_get(sync=true) is stateful.
